L0: A performance penalty metric that measures how much worse an automated helper does on the very first job of a fresh working session, used to quantify start-of-session ramp-up cost.
L1: A performance penalty metric that measures how much worse an automated helper does on the very first job of a fresh working session. It captures a ramp-up cost that shows up only on that first job because the helper has not yet worked out which of the group's several internal lookup tools or indexes is the authoritative one holding the data it needs. It is calculated as the score gap between that first job and the session's typical score, and this gap can be shrunk by loading the relevant tool-or-index fact into the session's memory at the start.
L2: A performance penalty metric measuring how much worse an automated helper does on the very first job of a fresh working session, quantifying start-of-session ramp-up cost. It exists because, at the start, the helper has not yet inferred which of the group's several internal lookup tools or indexes is authoritative and holds the needed data, so it needs a call or two to sort that out. It is measured as a point gap: the first job's score subtracted from the session's mean score (for example 12, 15, or 11 points under that mean). It applies only to the first job of a new session, never to later jobs in the same session, and the gap is not tied to how hard the job is, which was controlled for. Feeding the relevant tool-or-index fact into session memory upfront reduces it. The average gap is tracked each quarter and compared across periods, dropping from 15 points one quarter to 11 the next after a session-seeding change.
